answer: To defend against Sybil clusters, a topological cut audit checks network bottlenecks around suspected identities. Game-theoretic multi-agent auditors verify each identity commit against a verifiable random beacon. If topological cut verifications detect coordinated collusion, automated stake slashing destroys the adversary's bonded capital. Because auditors exchange an encrypted cipher of cross-verifications before reaching consensus at the summit, attacker cost scales superlinearly with cluster size.
